How Health Savings Accounts (HSAs) Create Long-Term Value for Highly Compensated Employees


7:33


Employers across industries are facing the same challenge: attracting great talent is difficult, and keeping it can be even harder.


While compensation remains important, today's highly compensated employees are evaluating a much broader picture. They want benefits that support not only their current financial well-being, but also their long-term security. As employers look for[meaningful ways to differentiate their benefits packages](https://www.bbsi.com/business-owner-resources/using-peo-offer-employee-health-insurance-could-be-the-best-investment-you-make-year) , they may want to consider the Health Savings Account (HSA) as a powerful yet underutilized component of a well-rounded benefits strategy.


Too often, HSAs are viewed simply as accounts that allow employees to pay medical expenses with pre-tax dollars. While that's certainly a valuable feature, limiting the conversation to tax savings misses the bigger opportunity.


For key employees and top performers, an HSA can become a long-term wealth accumulation vehicle, a retirement healthcare strategy, and a financial safety net during unexpected career transitions.


## What Are the Benefits of an HSA for Highly Compensated Employees?


Health Savings Accounts (HSAs) provide several benefits for highly compensated employees:


- Reduce taxable income through pre-tax contributions
- Allow investment earnings to grow tax-free
- Provide tax-free withdrawals for qualified medical expenses
- Help employees prepare for future healthcare costs
- Complement traditional retirement savings strategies
- Offer financial protection during employment transitions


Unlike Flexible Spending Accounts (FSAs), unused HSA balances roll over from year to year and can continue growing through investment earnings. For employees seeking additional ways to strengthen their financial future, an HSA can complement traditional retirement savings while providing valuable healthcare funding when it is needed most.


## Benefits That Matter Beyond Today


### How can an HSA support long-term financial security?


Highly compensated employees are often already maximizing contributions to retirement plans and seeking additional ways to build financial security. A Health Savings Account offers a unique opportunity because it combines immediate tax advantages with long-term investment potential. Contributions reduce taxable income, investment earnings grow tax-free, and qualified withdrawals remain tax-free.


Unlike a Flexible Spending Account (FSA), which is generally governed by "use-it-or-lose-it" rules, unused Health Savings Account balances roll over from year to year, helping employees build a dedicated fund for future healthcare needs.


For employees who can afford to pay current medical expenses from personal savings, the HSA can become less of a spending account and more of an investment account. Over time, invested HSA balances can accumulate alongside[traditional retirement assets](https://www.bbsi.com/business-owner-resources/state-mandated-retirement-plans) , helping employees prepare for future healthcare costs that are likely to increase throughout retirement.


## Retention Through Financial Wellness


### How can HSAs help employers attract and retain top talent?


Organizations spend significant resources recruiting talented employees. Yet many employers underestimate the impact that financial well-being programs can have on retention.


When an employer contributes to an employee's Health Savings Account, the message extends beyond healthcare. It demonstrates a commitment to helping employees build long-term financial resilience. For high-value employees, that contribution can represent an investment not only in their health, but also in their future.


[Benefits that create lasting value](https://www.bbsi.com/business-owner-resources/5-reasons-your-small-business-should-offer-health-insurance) tend to be more memorable than benefits that simply address short-term needs.


## Protection When Employees Need It Most


### How can an HSA provide financial protection during career transitions?


Another advantage that is rarely discussed is the role a Health Savings Account can play during unexpected life events.


A job loss, reduction in force, or long-term disability can create financial stress precisely when healthcare coverage becomes most important. Many employees are surprised to learn that HSA funds can be used tax-free to pay[COBRA premiums](https://www.bbsi.com/business-owner-resources/the-small-business-owners-guide-to-health-insurance-premiums) , allowing them to maintain coverage during a transition period.


For a key employee suddenly facing an employment disruption, a well-funded Health Savings Account can provide access to healthcare coverage without creating an additional tax burden. What may have started as a healthcare savings account becomes an important source of financial protection.


## A Competitive Advantage in the Talent Market


### Why should employers offer HSAs to highly compensated employees?


Employers are constantly evaluating which benefits provide the greatest return on investment. While many organizations focus on adding new programs, sometimes greater value comes from helping employees fully understand and utilize the benefits already available to them.


A Health Savings Account paired with a High Deductible Health Plan (HDHP) can deliver multiple forms of value for both employees and employers. The table below highlights how core HSA features translate into long-term benefits that support financial wellness, retention, and workforce stability.


HSA Feature


Long-Term Employee Benefit


Pre-tax contributions


Reduces taxable income


Tax-free investment growth


Supports long-term wealth accumulation


Tax-free qualified withdrawals


Helps cover healthcare expenses now and in retirement


Year-to-year rollover


Encourages long-term savings without "use-it-or-lose-it" pressure


COBRA premium eligibility


Provides financial protection during career transitions


Taken together, these features create a combination of immediate tax savings, long-term investment growth, retirement healthcare funding, and protection during employment transitions. In a labor market where[attracting and retaining top talent](https://www.bbsi.com/business-owner-resources/the-8-best-hiring-strategies-for-finding-and-retaining-good-employees) remains a priority, that's a value proposition worth discussing.


## Bottom Line


### Why are HSAs valuable for highly compensated employees?


The most successful benefit strategies don't simply help employees manage today's expenses. They help employees build confidence in tomorrow. For many highly compensated employees, a Health Savings Account may be one of the most powerful tools available to accomplish both.

## Frequently Asked Questions About HSAs


##### Can HSA funds be invested?


Yes. Depending on the provider, HSA balances can often be invested in mutual funds and other investment options, allowing funds to grow over time and potentially support future healthcare and retirement-related expenses.


##### Are HSA funds lost at the end of the year?


No. Unlike many Flexible Spending Accounts, HSA balances roll over from year to year. Unused funds remain in the account and continue to belong to the employee.


##### Can HSA funds be used for COBRA premiums?


Yes. Eligible HSA funds can generally be used tax-free to pay COBRA premiums, helping employees maintain healthcare coverage during employment transitions.


##### What happens to an HSA if an employee leaves a company?


A Health Savings Account belongs to the employee, not the employer. Employees keep their HSA and any accumulated funds when they change jobs or leave a company.


##### Why do employers offer Health Savings Accounts?


Many employers offer Health Savings Accounts because they provide employees with tax advantages, long-term savings opportunities, and financial flexibility for healthcare expenses. HSAs can also strengthen an employer's overall benefits strategy and support talent attraction and retention efforts.
